rationale: The round-0 candidate built, ran, and preserved correctness with no ICE fallback, so this round raises obfuscation pressure rather than retreating. fasta is a tiny two-function program dominated by one compute-dense main with tight hot loops, so per-pass weights emphasize control-flow and arithmetic transforms that survive well on a single large function while keeping runtime-cost weights elevated enough to protect loop throughput: SUB stays cheap and near-always applicable (high SecurityGain/DiversityGain, minimal RuntimeCost), BCF and FLA are pushed higher as the primary defenses since opaque predicates and control-flow flattening give the most resistance on one big function body, and SPLIT is kept moderately weighted to feed FLA more basic blocks to flatten, increasing its effectiveness on a program with few functions. IBR, ICALL, and IGV get mid-range security weights with noticeably higher runtime-cost weights because indirect branches, indirect calls, and global-variable indirection pay off less on a two-function program with very few call sites and globals, and their dispatch overhead lands directly in main's hot loop; keeping their RuntimeCost weights around 0.25-0.45 lets the selector apply them only where features strongly favor them. CorrectnessRisk stays low across the board since round 0 showed no instability, but is not zeroed to preserve a safety margin for the more semantics-touching passes (FLA, ICALL).
